A.subject: Physics
A.text: The radii of two planets 'A' and 'B' are 'R' and '4R' and their densities are ρ and ρ/3 respectively. The ratio of acceleration due to gravity at their surfaces (g_A : g_B) will be:
A.sol_text: g ∝ ρR. For planet A: g_A ∝ ρ × R. For planet B: g_B ∝ (ρ/3) × 4R. Therefore, g_A/g_B = (ρ × R)/((ρ/3) × 4R) = (1 × 3)/(1 × 4) = 3/4. Thus g_A : g_B = 3 : 4

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The free space inside a current carrying toroid is filled with a material of susceptibility 2 × 10^(-2). The percentage increase in the value of magnetic field inside the toroid will be:
A.sol_text: The relationship between magnetic field change and susceptibility is: ΔB/B₀ = χ. Given χ = 2 × 10^(-2), the percentage increase is: (ΔB/B₀) × 100 = (2 × 10^(-2)) × 100 = 2%

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Three vessels of equal volume contain gases at the same temperature and pressure. The first vessel contains neon (monatomic), the second contains chlorine (diatomic) and third contains uranium hexafluoride (polyatomic). Arrange these on the basis of their root mean square speed (v_rms) and choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A.sol_text: v_rms is same for all, if mass and temperature is same. v_rms is proportional to 1/sqrt(M). Since v_poly < v_dia < v_mono, we have v_rms (mono) > v_rms (dia) > v_rms (poly). The root mean square speed depends on molar mass inversely. Neon has smallest molar mass (20 g/mol), chlorine has intermediate molar mass (71 g/mol), and uranium hexafluoride has largest molar mass (352 g/mol). Therefore v_rms (mono) > v_rms (dia) > v_rms (poly).

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two radioactive elements A and B initially have same number of atoms. The half life of A is same as the average life of B. If λA and λB are decay constants of A and B respectively, then choose the correct relation from the given options.
A.sol_text: Half-life of A: t(1/2)A = ln2/λA. Average life of B: τB = 1/λB. Given: t(1/2)A = τB, so ln2/λA = 1/λB. Therefore, λA = λB ln2

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The electric field in an electromagnetic wave is given as E = 20 sin(ω(t - x/c)) j NC^(-1) where ω and c are angular frequency and velocity of electromagnetic wave respectively. The energy contained in a volume of 5 × 10^(-4) m^3 will be (Given ε₀ = 8.85 × 10^(-12) C^2/Nm^2)

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
A.text: A metallic surface is illuminated with radiation of wavelength λ, the stopping potential is V₀. If the same surface is illuminated with radiation of wavelength 2λ, the stopping potential becomes V₀/4. The threshold wavelength for this metallic surface will be:
A.sol_text: Using photoelectric equation: V₀ = hc/λ₀ - φ for wavelength λ. For wavelength 2λ: V₀/4 = hc/(2λ₀) - φ. Subtracting: V₀ - V₀/4 = hc/λ₀ - hc/(2λ₀), which gives 3V₀/4 = hc/(2λ₀). From first equation: φ = hc/λ₀ - V₀. At threshold, stopping potential = 0, so hc/λ_th = φ = 3V₀/2. Since hc/λ₀ = 3V₀/2, we get λ_th = 2hc/(3V₀) = (1/2) × (2hc/3λ₀) × (λ/λ) = λ/3. Wait, recalculating: hc/λ_th = (1/2) × (2hc)/(3λ₀). Since hc/λ = 3V₀/2 from the algebra, λ_th = (3V₀/2) × (2/(hc/λ)) = 3λ.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two identical heater filaments are connected first in parallel and then in series. At the same applied voltage, the ratio of heat produced in same time for parallel to series will be:
A.sol_text: For series connection: Two resistances R in series give total resistance 2R. Heat produced P1 = V^2/(2R). For parallel connection: Two resistances R in parallel give equivalent resistance R/2. Heat produced P2 = V^2/(R/2) = 2V^2/R. Ratio P2/P1 = (2V^2/R)/(V^2/2R) = (2V^2/R) × (2R/V^2) = 4/1 = 4:1

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Form the v-t graph shown, the ratio of distance to displacement in 25 s of motion is:
A.sol_text: From the v-t graph, calculate the net area (displacement) and total distance. Area = (1/2 × 5 × 10) + (5 + 10) + (1/2 × 30 × 5) + (1/2 × 20 × 5) - (1/2 × 20 × 5) = 25 + 50 + 75 + 50 - 50. Net area = Displacement = 150 m. Distance = (200 + 50) = 250 m. Ratio = distance/displacement = 250/150 = 5/3.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The current sensitivity of moving coil galvanometer is increased by 25%. This increase is achieved only changing in the number of turns of coils and area of cross section of the wire while keeping the resistance of galvanometer coil constant. The percentage change in the voltage sensitivity will be:
A.sol_text: Current sensitivity S_I = hBA/k. Voltage sensitivity S_V = (nAB)/(kR). Since R is constant and S_I increases by 25%, we have ΔS_I = (ΔS_V). The change (ΔS_V) = +25%. Therefore voltage sensitivity increases by 25%.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A coin placed on a rotating table just slips when it is placed at a distance of 1 cm from the centre. If the angular velocity of the table is halved, it will just slip when placed at a distance of _____ from the centre:
A.sol_text: For a coin to slip on a rotating table, the centripetal force required equals the maximum static friction. f = m*omega^2*r. At the point of slipping: m*omega^2*r = mu*m*g, so omega^2*r = constant. Initially: omega^2 * 1 = constant. When omega is halved: (omega/2)^2 * r' = omega^2 * 1, which gives (omega^2/4) * r' = omega^2 * 1, so r' = 4 cm.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A transmitting antenna is kept on the surface of the earth. The minimum height of receiving antenna required to receive the signal in line of sight at 4 km distance from it is x × 10^-2 m. The value of x is ___. (Let, radius of earth R = 6400 km)
A.sol_text: Using the formula for line of sight communication: y = sqrt(2Rh), where h is height and R is radius of earth. Given distance d = 4 km = 4 × 10^3 m. For line of sight: d = sqrt(2Rh). Squaring: (4 × 10^3)^2 = 2 × 6400000 × h. 16 × 10^6 = 2 × 64 × 10^5 × h. h = (16 × 10^6)/(2 × 64 × 10^5) = 160/(2 × 64) × 10 m = 1000/8 × 10^-2 m = 125 × 10^-2 m. Therefore x = 125.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: 1 kg of water at 100°C is converted into steam at 100°C by boiling at atmospheric pressure. The volume of water changes from 1.00 × 10^(-3) m³ as a liquid to 1.671 m³ as steam. The change in internal energy of the system during the process will be (Given latent heat of vaporisation = 2257 kJ/kg, Atmospheric pressure = 1 × 10^5 Pa)
A.sol_text: Work done = P × (V_final - V_initial) = 1 × 10^5 × (1.671 - 0.001) m³ = 1.670 × 10^5 J. Heat supplied Q = latent heat × mass = 2257 × 1 × 10^3 J = 22.57 × 10^5 J. Change in internal energy ΔU = Q - W = (22.57 - 1.67) × 10^5 J = 20.9 × 10^5 J = 2090 kJ

A.subject: Physics
A.text: On a temperature scale 'X', the boiling point of water is 65°X and the freezing point is -15°X. Assuming that the X scale is linear. The equivalent temperature corresponding to -95°X on the Fahrenheit scale would be:
A.sol_text: Set up linear relationship between X and Fahrenheit scales. At boiling point: 65°X = 212°F. At freezing point: -15°X = 32°F. Using these two points, find the conversion formula: (65 - X')/(65 + 15) = (212 - F)/(212 - 32). This gives (65 + 95)/80 = (212 - F)/180. So 160/80 = (212 - F)/180, which means 2 × 180 = 212 - F, therefore F = 212 - 360 = -148°F.

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
A.text: The logic performed by the circuit shown in figure is equivalent to
A.sol_text: Analyzing the circuit: The first stage has two NOR gates (one with input a, one with input b). NOR of a single input gives (A̅) and (B̅). These outputs go to an OR gate. Therefore: Output = (A̅) + (B̅) = (AB)̅ = (AB) AND gate by De Morgan's law. This is equivalent to an AND gate operation.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: As per the given graph, choose the correct representation for curve A and curve B {Where Xc = Reactance of pure capacitive circuit connected with A.C. source, XL = Reactance of pure inductive circuit connected with A.C. source, R = Impedance of pure resistive circuit connected with A.C. source, Z = Impedance of the LCR series circuit}
A.sol_text: From the graph, Curve A decreases with frequency (inversely proportional), which matches Xc = 1/(ωC). Curve B increases with frequency (directly proportional), which matches XL = ωL. Therefore, A = Xc and B = XL.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: An average force of 125 N is applied on a machine gun firing bullets each of mass 10 g at the speed of 250 m/s to keep it in position. The number of bullets fired per second by the machine gun is:
A.sol_text: Using F = n(mv), where F is force, n is number of bullets per second, m is mass of each bullet, and v is velocity. Given: F = 125 N, m = 10 g = 10/1000 = 0.01 kg, v = 250 m/s. Therefore: 125 = n × 0.01 × 250 = n × 2.5. Solving: n = 125/2.5 = 50 bullets per second.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The variation of kinetic energy (KE) of a particle executing simple harmonic motion with the displacement (x) starting from mean position to extreme position (A) is given by:
options: Graph (1): Linear increase from 0 to A
Graph (2): Constant KE from 0 to A
Graph (3): Curved decrease from maximum to 0 at A
Graph (4): Curved increase from 0 to maximum at A
A.sol_text: For simple harmonic motion, K.E. = (1/2)m(A^2 - x^2). At mean position (x=0), K.E. is maximum = (1/2)mA^2. At extreme position (x=A), K.E. = 0. The relationship is quadratic: K.E. decreases as x increases from 0 to A, following a curved path (parabolic). This matches graph (3) which shows a downward curving function from maximum to zero.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The critical angle for a denser-rarer interface is 45°. The speed of light in rarer medium is 3 × 10^8 m/s. The speed of light in the denser medium is:
A.sol_text: At critical angle θc, sin(θc) = 1/μ where μ is refractive index. Given θc = 45°, so sin(45°) = 1/√2 = 1/μ, therefore μ = √2. The speed of light in denser medium is v = c/μ = (3 × 10^8)/√2 = 2.12 × 10^8 m/s

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 2 F is charged to a potential V. The energy stored in the capacitor is E1. The capacitor is now connected to another uncharged identical capacitor in parallel combination. The energy stored in the combination is E2. The ratio E2/E1 is:
A.sol_text: Initial energy: E1 = (1/2) × 2 × V^2 = V^2. When two identical capacitors are connected in parallel, total capacitance = 2 + 2 = 4 F. By charge conservation: Q = 2V = 2V' + 2V', so V' = V/2. Final energy: E2 = (1/2) × 4 × (V/2)^2 = (1/2) × 4 × V^2/4 = V^2/2. Therefore, E2/E1 = (V^2/2)/V^2 = 1/2, which is ratio 1:2.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Astronomical unit (Au), Parsec (Pc) and Light year (ly) are units for measuring astronomical distances. Statement II: Au < Parsec (Pc) < ly. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statements I and Statements II are incorrect
Statements I is correct but Statements II is incorrect
Both Statements I and Statements II are correct
Statements I is incorrect but Statements II is correct
A.sol_text: Statement I is correct: Au, Parsec (Pc), and Light year (ly) are all units for measuring astronomical distances. Statement II is incorrect: The correct order is Au < ly < Parsec. From the solution: 1 Parsec = 2 × 10^5 Au, 1 Au = 1.58 × 10^-5 ly, and 1 Au < ly < Parsec. Therefore, Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A force F = (2 + 3x) i acts on a particle in the x direction where F is in newton and x is in meter. The work done by this force during a displacement from x = 0 to x = 4 m, is _______ J.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: The magnetic field B crossing normally a square metallic plate of area 4 m^2 is changing with time as shown in figure. The magnitude of induced emf in the plate during t = 2 s to t = 4 s, is _______ mV.
B.sol_text: Using Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction: emf = -d(phi)/dt = -A * dB/dt. From the graph, during t = 2 s to t = 4 s: B changes from 4 mT to 8 mT, so dB/dt = (8-4)/(4-2) = 4/2 = 2 mT/s = 0.002 T/s. Area A = 4 m^2. Therefore, emf = A * |dB/dt| = 4 * 0.002 = 0.008 V = 8 mV.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: The length of a wire becomes l₁ and l₂ when 100 N and 120 N tension are applied respectively. If 10l₂ = 11l₁, then the natural length of wire will be (1/x)l₁. Here the value of x is
B.sol_text: Using stress-strain relationship: F/A = Y(Δl/l) and Δl = (FL)/(AY). For the wire under tension F₁ = 100 N and F₂ = 120 N: l₁ = (F₁/(AY) + 1)L and l₂ = (F₂/(AY) + 1)L. Given 10l₂ = 11l₁, substituting and simplifying: 10[120/(AY) + 1]L = 11[100/(AY) + 1]L. This gives 1200/(AY) + 10 = 1100/(AY) + 11, so 100/(AY) = 1, meaning AY = 100. Therefore L = l₁/[100/(AY) + 1] = l₁/(100/100 + 1) = l₁/2 = (1/2)l₁. Thus x = 2.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A monochromatic light is incident on a hydrogen sample in ground state. Hydrogen atoms absorb a fraction of light and subsequently emit radiation of six different wavelengths. The frequency of incident light is x × 10^15 Hz. The value of x is _______. (Given h = 4.25 × 10^-15 eVs)
B.sol_text: If n(n-1)/2 = 6, then n = 6. For hydrogen atom, transition from n=6 to n=1 gives: Δe = 13.6(1/1 - 1/36) = 13.6 × 35/36 eV. Using hf = E, f = (13.6 × 35)/(36 × 4.25 × 10^-15) = 3 × 10^15 Hz. Therefore x = 3.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I Species: A. H2O, B. Acetylide anion, C. NH4+, D. ClO2-. List-II Geometry/Shape: I. Tetrahedral, II. Linear, III. Pyramidal, IV. Bent
A.sol_text: H2O has 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs → Bent geometry (III). Acetylide ion (C2(2-)) is linear → Linear (II). NH4+ has 4 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs → Tetrahedral (I). ClO2- has 2 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair → Bent (IV). Therefore: A(III), B(II), C(I), D(IV)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Find out the correct statement from the options given below for the above 2 reactions. Reaction (I): 4-methoxybenzyl chloride + Nu → 4-methoxybenzyl Nu. Reaction (II): 4-nitrobenzyl chloride + Nu → 4-nitrobenzyl Nu. Where Nu = Nucleophile
options: Reaction (I) is of 2nd order and reaction (II) is of 1st order
Reactions (I) and (II) both are of 2nd order
Reactions (I) is of 1st order and reaction (II) is of 2nd order
Reaction (I) and (II) both are of 1st order
A.sol_text: Reaction (I): The methoxy group (-OMe) is electron-donating and stabilizes the carbocation intermediate formed during SN1 mechanism, making it a 1st order reaction (SN1 pathway). Reaction (II): The nitro group (-NO2) is electron-withdrawing and does not stabilize the carbocation intermediate. The reaction proceeds via SN2 mechanism, making it a 2nd order reaction (SN2 pathway). Therefore, reaction (I) is 1st order and reaction (II) is 2nd order.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: For compound having the formula GaAlCl4, the correct option from the following is:
options: Ga is coordinated with Cl in GaAlCl4
Ga is more electronegative than Al and is present as a cationic part of the salt GaAlCl4
Cl forms bond with both Al and Ga in GaAlCl4
Oxidation state of Ga in the salt GaAlCl4 is +3.
A.sol_text: GaAlCl4 exists as Ga+ [AlCl4]-. Although Ga is more electronegative than Al, in this compound Ga acts as the cationic part while AlCl4- acts as the anionic part. This is because Ga+ is formed and acts as a cation despite higher electronegativity, making option (2) correct.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: L-isomer of tetrose X(C4H6O4) gives positive Schiff's test and has two chiral carbons. On acetylation 'X' yields triacetate. 'X' also undergoes following reactions. 'A' + HNO3 → 'X' + NaBH4 → 'B' (Chiral compound). Identify the structure of X from the given options (1), (2), (3), (4).
options: Structure with CHO at top, H-OH, H-OH, O with CH2OH at bottom
Structure with CHO at top, H-OH, HO-H, CH2OH at bottom
Structure with H-OH, HO-OH, O with CH2OH at bottom
Structure with CHO at top, HO-H, HO-H, CH2OH at bottom
A.sol_text: X is a tetrose (C4H6O4) with positive Schiff's test indicating an aldehyde group. It has two chiral carbons. Oxidation with HNO3 gives a dicarboxylic acid. Reduction with NaBH4 converts the aldehyde to primary alcohol yielding a chiral compound. The structure must be an L-isomer of erythrose or threose. Based on the Fischer projections and the requirement of two chiral centers with specific stereochemistry, option (2) represents L-erythrose with CHO group, and the correct stereochemistry at both chiral centers.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I: A. K, B. KCl, C. KOH, D. Li; List-II: I. Thermonuclear reactions, II. Fertilizer, III. Sodium potassium pump, IV. Absorbent of CO2
A.sol_text: Lithium (Li) is used in thermonuclear reactions. K+ ions are used in sodium potassium pump. KOH is an absorbent of CO2. KCl is used as fertilizer. Therefore: A→I, B→II, C→IV, D→III which corresponds to option (1): A(III), B(II), C(IV), D(I) - Note: The matching should be D→I (Li→Thermonuclear), A→III (K→Na-K pump), C→IV (KOH→CO2 absorbent), B→II (KCl→Fertilizer).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: o-Phenylenediamine 'X' reacts with HNO2 to give 'X' Major Product
options: diazonium diazo structure with N+=N and N2+
aminobenzene diazonium structure with N2+ and NH2
A.sol_text: o-Phenylenediamine has two adjacent amino groups on benzene ring. When treated with HNO2 (nitrous acid), one amino group is converted to diazonium group (N2+) while the other remains as NH2. The diazonium group then undergoes intramolecular nucleophilic attack by the adjacent NH2 group on the benzene ring, followed by loss of N2 and deprotonation to form benzotriazole (option 1), which is a stable aromatic heterocycle.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: 25 mL of silver nitrate solution (1M) is added dropwise to 25 mL of potassium iodide (1.05 M) solution. The ion(s) present in very small quantity in the solution is/are:
A.sol_text: millimoles of AgNO3 = 25, millimoles of KI = 25 × 1.05 = 26.25. Since KI is in excess and AgI forms negatively charged colloid, some Ag+ remains in solution. Ions Ag+ and I- are therefore present in very small quantity.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of rate of aromatic electrophilic substitution reaction.
A.sol_text: The rate of aromatic electrophilic substitution depends on the activating/deactivating nature of substituents. Compound c has a carbonyl group (deactivating, electron-withdrawing) - slowest. Compound a has OH on sp3 carbon (moderate activation). Compound b has OH on sp2 carbon (ortho to benzene, better activation). Compound d has OH with oxygen in ether linkage and oxygen on sp2 carbon (strongest activation due to resonance). Order: c < a < b < d

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The complex that dissolves in water is
A.sol_text: [Fe3(OH)2(OAc)6]Cl dissolves in water. Rest of the complexes form precipitate (ppt).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The polymer X-consists of linear molecules and is closely packed. It is prepared in the presence of triethylaluminium and titanium tetrachloride under low pressure. The polymer X is
A.sol_text: High density polythene (HDPE) is prepared using Ziegler-Natta catalyst (triethylaluminium and titanium tetrachloride) under low pressure. This catalyst enables stereospecific polymerization of ethylene, producing linear molecules that are closely packed, resulting in high density polythene.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The set which does not have ambidentate ligand(s) is:
A.sol_text: An ambidentate ligand is one that can coordinate to a metal center through two different atoms. C2O4^2- (oxalate) is ambidentate as it can coordinate through O or C. Ethylenediamine is not ambidentate - it coordinates through two N atoms. H2O is not ambidentate - it coordinates only through O. Therefore, option (1) contains non-ambidentate ligands (ethylenediamine and H2O), making it the set without ambidentate ligand(s).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: When a solution of mixture having two inorganic salts was treated with freshly prepared ferrous sulphate in acidic medium, a dark brown ring was formed whereas on treatment with neutral FeCl3, it gave deep red colour which disappeared on boiling and a brown red ppt was formed. The mixture contains
A.sol_text: Dark brown ring is formed in the confirmatory test of NO3^- ions (brown ring test with FeSO4 in acidic medium). Deep red ppt with FeCl3 is formed in the presence of CH3COO^- ions (acetate ions form deep red colour with FeCl3 which disappears on boiling and forms brown red ppt). Therefore, the mixture contains CH3COO^- & NO3^-.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement-I: Methane and steam passed over a heated Ni catalyst produces hydrogen gas. Statement-II: Sodium nitrite reacts with NH4Cl to give H2O, N2 and NaCl. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both the statements I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both the statements I and II are correct
A.sol_text: Statement I is correct as CH4 and steam in presence of Ni catalyst forms water gas (CO + H2). Statement II is also correct as NaNO2 + NH4Cl → N2 + NaCl + H2O, or NH4NO2 → N2 + H2O

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement-I: If BOD is 4 ppm and dissolved oxygen is 8 ppm, then it is a good quality water. Statement-II: If the concentration of zinc and nitrate salts are 5 ppm each, then it can be a good quality water. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both the statements I and II are incorrect
Both the statements I and II are correct
A.sol_text: BOD < 5 ppm for clean water. Here BOD is 4 ppm which is acceptable. Dissolved oxygen > 6 ppm is acceptable for water, here it is 8 ppm which is acceptable. Threshold concentration for NO3 is 50 ppm, here it is 5 ppm which is acceptable. Zn concentration is 5 ppm which is at the threshold limit and acceptable. Hence, water is of good quality. Both statements are correct.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
A.text: In the extraction process of copper, the product obtained after carrying out the reactions (i) 2Cu2S + 3O2 → 2Cu2O + 2SO2 and (ii) 2Cu2O + Cu2S → 6Cu + SO2 is called
A.sol_text: The reactions given are carried out in the production of blister copper using self reduction. In this process, Cu2S (copper sulfide) is first oxidized to Cu2O in the presence of oxygen, and then Cu2O reacts with remaining Cu2S to produce copper metal. The product obtained is called blister copper because it contains gas bubbles trapped in the copper metal.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: In the photoelectric effect, the electrons are ejected from the metal surface as soon as the beam of light of frequency greater than threshold frequency strikes the surface. Reason R: When the photon of any energy strikes an electron in the atom, transfer of energy from the photon to the electron takes place. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
A.sol_text: A is correct as electrons are ejected when incident frequency > threshold frequency. R is incorrect because not any photon of any energy can cause ionization; the photon must have energy greater than or equal to the work function. R incorrectly states that any photon can transfer energy, when in reality only photons with sufficient energy cause photoelectric effect.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: For elements B, C, N Li, Be, O and F, the correct order of first ionization enthalpy is:
options: Li < Be < B < C < O < N < F
B < Li < Be < C < N < O < F
Li < Be < B < C < N < O < F
Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F
A.sol_text: The correct order of 1st ionization energy is: Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F. This follows the general trend of increasing ionization energy across a period with exceptions: Be (completely filled 2s orbital) > B, and N (half-filled 2p orbital) > O due to extra stability.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which of the following complex has a possibility to exist as meridional isomer?
A.sol_text: [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] can show facial and meridional isomerism because it has three monodentate ligands of each type (3 NH3 and 3 NO2) attached to an octahedral center. This allows for different spatial arrangements - facial (all three of one type on one face) and meridional (three ligands along a meridian line) isomers. The other complexes cannot show this type of isomerism.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Thin layer chromatography of a mixture shows the following observation: A, B, C are three spots on TLC plate. The correct order of elution in the silica gel column chromatography is:
A.sol_text: In TLC, compounds that travel farther (higher Rf values) are less polar and elute first in column chromatography. From the chromatogram, the order of increasing Rf values is: B < A < C. In silica gel column chromatography with non-polar solvent, less polar compounds elute first. Therefore, the elution order is A > C > B, which corresponds to option (3) A, C, B.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: A mixture of y mole of an aldehyde with x mole of MeMgBr is treated with H3O+. The ratio x/y on completion of the above reaction is ____.
B.sol_text: The reaction involves MeMgBr (methylmagnesium bromide) reacting with an aldehyde. The aldehyde (1 mole) requires: 1 mole of MeMgBr for nucleophilic addition to form a secondary alcohol (RCH2-OH after protonation), and 1 additional mole of MeMgBr to deprotonate the hydroxyl group (acid-base reaction). Therefore, 2 moles of MeMgBr are needed per mole of aldehyde. For y moles of aldehyde, x = 2y, so x/y = 2.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: Solid fuel used in rocket is a mixture of Fe2O3 and Al (in ratio 1 : 2). The heat evolved (kJ) per gram of the mixture is _____ (Nearest integer). Given: ΔHf°(Al2O3) = -1700 kJ mol^(-1), ΔHf°(Fe2O3) = -840 kJ mol^(-1). Molar mass of Fe, Al and O are 56, 27 and 16 g mol^(-1) respectively
B.sol_text: Balanced equation: Fe2O3 + 2Al → 2Fe + Al2O3. ΔH°reaction = -1700 + 840 = -860 kJ. Mass ratio of Fe2O3:Al = 160:54 = 2.96 in 214 gm mixture. Heat per gram = -860/214 ≈ -4 kJ/gram
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The ratio of spin-only magnetic moment values μ_eff[Cr(CN)6]^3−/μ_eff[Cr(H2O)6]^3+ is ______.
B.sol_text: μ_eff of [Cr(CN)6]^3− = sqrt(15) BM. μ_eff of [Cr(H2O)6]^3+ = sqrt(15) BM. Ratio = sqrt(15)/sqrt(15) = 1

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: 0.004 M K2SO4 solution is isotonic with 0.01 M glucose solution. Percentage dissociation of K2SO4 is _____ (Nearest integer)
B.sol_text: As osmotic pressures are equal, we have (0.004) × i = 0.01. For K2SO4: i = 0.01/0.004 = 10/4 = 5/2 = 1 + 2α. Therefore 2α = 1.5, α = 0.75, % α = 75%
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: KClO3 + 6FeSO4 + 3H2SO4 → KCl + 3Fe2(SO4)3 + 3H2O. The above reaction was studied at 300 K by monitoring the concentration of FeSO4 in which initial concentration was 10 M and after half an hour became 8.8 M. The rate of production of Fe2(SO4)3 is _______ × 10^-6 mol L^-1 s^-1. (Nearest integer)
B.sol_text: Rate of decomposition of FeSO4 = (10 - 8.8)/(30 × 3600) = (1.2 × 60)/(3600 × 30) mol L^-1 s^-1. From stoichiometry, 6 FeSO4 produces 3 Fe2(SO4)3, so rate of production of Fe2(SO4)3 = (1/2) × rate of FeSO4 decomposition = (0.6 × 60)/(3600 × 30) = 3.33 × 10^-4 = 333.3 × 10^-6 mol L^-1 s^-1 ≈ 333 × 10^-6 mol L^-1 s^-1
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let f:[2,4] → R be a differentiable function such that (x log_e x)f'(x) + (log_e x)f(x) + f(x) ≥ 1, x ∈ [2,4] with f(2) = 1/2 and f(4) = 1/2. Consider the following two statements: (A) f(x) ≤ 1, for all x ∈ [2,4] (B) f(x) ≥ 1/8, for all x ∈ [2,4]
options: Neither statement (A) nor statement (B) is true
Both the statements (A) and (B) are true
A.sol_text: From the given differential inequality, we derive d[x ln f(x) - x] ≥ 0 OR d[x ln(f(x))] ≥ 1. Define h(x) = x ln f(x) - x. Then h(x) ≥ h(2) for x ∈ [2,4], giving x ln f(x) - x ≥ 2 ln2f(2) - 2. Using boundary conditions f(2) = f(4) = 1/2, we get: x ln f(x) - x ≥ 2 ln2 - 2 and x ln f(x) - x ≤ ln4 - 4. This yields (ln2-2)/(x ln x) + 1/(ln x) ≤ f(x) ≤ (ln4-4)/(x ln x) + 1/(ln x). From these bounds: f(x) ≤ 1 and f(x) ≥ 1/8. However, LMVT on f(x)·x ln x cannot be simultaneously satisfied, meaning no such f(x) exists satisfying all constraints. Both inequalities are mathematically derived but the function itself cannot exist.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let R be a rectangle given by the lines x = 0, x = 2, y = 0 and y = 5. Let A(alpha, 0) and B(0, beta), alpha in [0, 2] and beta in [0, 5], be such that the line segment AB divides the area of the rectangle R in the ratio 4:1. Then, the mid-point of AB lies on a
A.sol_text: Rectangle R has area = 2 × 5 = 10. Line AB divides it in ratio 4:1, so one part has area 8 and other has area 2. The triangle formed by A(alpha, 0), B(0, beta), and origin has area = (1/2)×alpha×beta. This equals 2, so alpha×beta = 4. Mid-point P of AB is (alpha/2, beta/2). Let h = alpha/2 and k = beta/2, then alpha = 2h and beta = 2k. From alpha×beta = 4, we get 4hk = 4, so xy = 1 (where x = h, y = k). This is the equation of a hyperbola.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let S = {M = [aij], aij ∈ {0, 1, 2}, {1 ≤ i, j ≤ 2}} be a sample space and A:{M ∈ S :M is invertible} be an even. Then P(A) is equal to
A.sol_text: If M is invertible, then |M| ≠ 0. For |M| = 0: matrices like [[1,1],[1,1]], [[0,0],[0,0]], [[2,2],[2,2]] give total 3 matrices. Matrices with two 1's and two 0's, two 2's and two 0's, two 1's and two 2's each give 4 matrices. One 1 and three 0's gives 4, one 2 and three 0's gives 4. One 1, one 2, and two 0's gives 8 matrices. Total matrices with |M| = 0 is 31. Total sample space = 3^4 = 81. P(A) = 1 - 31/81 = 50/81

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The number of integral solution x of log_{x+7/2}((x-7)/(2x-3))^2 ≥ 0 is:
A.sol_text: Find domain: x + 7/2 > 0 and x + 7/2 ≠ 1 and (x-7)/(2x-3) ≠ 0. This gives x > -7/2, x ≠ -5/2, x ≠ 7, x ≠ 3/2. Case 1: When 0 < x + 7/2 < 1, i.e., -7/2 < x < -5/2, the inequality becomes ((x-7)/(2x-3))^2 ≤ 1, which gives -1 ≤ (x-7)/(2x-3) ≤ 1. Solving yields -7/2 < x < -5/2 (no integers). Case 2: When x + 7/2 > 1, i.e., x > -5/2, the inequality becomes ((x-7)/(2x-3))^2 ≥ 1, which gives (x-7)/(2x-3) ≤ -1 or (x-7)/(2x-3) ≥ 1. This gives x ∈ [-4, 3/2) ∪ (3/2, 10/3]. Combined with domain restrictions and x > -5/2: x ∈ (-5/2, 3/2) ∪ (3/2, 10/3]. The integers in this range are: -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3. Total = 6 integers.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let A be a 2 × 2 matrix with real entries such that A' = αA + I, where α ∈ R − {−1, 1}. If det(A^2 − A) = 4, the sum of all possible values of α is equal to:
A.sol_text: Let A = [a b; c d]. From A' = αA + I, we get A^T = αA + I. Comparing entries: a = αa + 1, so a = 1/(1−α); b = αc; c = αb; d = αd + 1, so d = 1/(1−α). From b = αc and c = αb: if b,c ≠ 0, then α = ±1 (not allowed). Therefore c = 0, b = 0. Now det(A^2 − A) = 4 gives |A||A − I| = 4. With a = d = 1/(1−α), we get (1/(1−α))^2 · (1/(1−α) − 1)^2 = 4, which simplifies to (1/(1−α))^2 · (α/(1−α))^2 = 4. This gives 1/(1−α)^4 · α^2 = 4, leading to α = 1/2 or α = 2. Sum = 1/2 + 2 = 5/2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The value of the integral ∫[from -log_e(2) to log_e(2)] e^x [log_e(e^x + √(1+e^(2x)))] dx is equal to:
A.sol_text: Substitute e^x = t, so e^x dx = dt. When x = -log(2), t = 1/2; when x = log(2), t = 2. The integral becomes ∫[1/2 to 2] log_e(t + √(1+t^2)) dt. Using integration by parts and evaluating: [t·ln(√(t^2+1)+t) - √(t^2+1)]|_[1/2 to 2]. After simplification and algebraic manipulation, the result is log_e(√2(2+√5)^2/√(1+√5)) - √5/2

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let sets A and B have 5 elements each. Let the mean of the elements in sets A and B be 5 and 8 respectively and the variance of the elements in sets A and B be 12 and 20 respectively. A new set C of 10 elements is formed by subtracting 3 from each element of A and adding 2 to each element of B. Then the sum of the mean and variance of the elements of C is
A.sol_text: For set A: mean = 5, variance = 12. After subtracting 3 from each element: new mean = 5 - 3 = 2, variance remains 12. For set B: mean = 8, variance = 20. After adding 2 to each element: new mean = 8 + 2 = 10, variance remains 20. Combined mean of C = (5×2 + 5×10)/10 = 60/10 = 6. Combined variance = [5×12 + 5×20]/10 - (6-6)^2 = [60 + 100]/10 = 160/10 = 16. Wait, recalculating: Variance of C = [sum(x_i - 3)^2 + sum(y_i + 2)^2]/10 - (mean_C)^2 = [80 + 600]/10 - 36 = 68 - 36 = 32. Sum = mean + variance = 6 + 32 = 38.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let (α, β, γ) be the image of point P(2, 3, 5) in the plane 2x + y - 3z = 6. Then α + β + γ is equal to:
A.sol_text: The image of point P(2,3,5) in plane 2x+y-3z=6 is found using the reflection formula. The normal vector is (2,1,-3). Using the formula (α-2)/2 = (β-3)/1 = (γ-5)/(-3) = -2(4+3-15-6)/14 = 2. This gives: α-2=2⟹α=6, β-3=2⟹β=5, γ-5=-6⟹γ=-1. Therefore α+β+γ=6+5-1=10.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let f(x) = [x^2 - x] + |-x + [x]|, where x ∈ R and [t] denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to t. Then, f is:
options: continuous at x = 0, but not continuous at x = 1
continuous at x = 1, but not continuous at x = 0
not continuous at x = 0 and x = 1
A.sol_text: f(x) = [x^2 - x] + |x - [x]| = [x^2 - x] + {x}, where {x} ≥ 0 is the fractional part. At x = 0: f(0) = 0, f(0-) = -1, so discontinuous at x = 0. At x = 1: f(1) = 0, f(1+) = 0, f(1-) = 0, so continuous at x = 1. Option (2) is correct.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: For any vector a = a1 i + a2 j + a3 k, with 10|ai| < 1, i = 1, 2, 3, consider the following statements: (A): max{|a1|, |a2|, |a3|} ≤ a (B): |a| ≤ 3 max{|a1|, |a2|, |a3|}
A.sol_text: |a| = sqrt(a1^2 + a2^2 + a3^2) ≥ max{|a1|, |a2|, |a3|}, so Statement A is true. Also, |a| = sqrt(a1^2 + a2^2 + a3^2) ≤ sqrt(3*max(a1^2, a2^2, a3^2)) ≤ 3*max{|a1|, |a2|, |a3|}, so Statement B is true. Therefore, both (A) and (B) are true.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Area of the region {(x, y) : x^2 + (y - 2)^2 ≤ 4, x^2 ≥ 2y} is:
A.sol_text: The region is bounded by circle x^2 + (y - 2)^2 ≤ 4 (center at (0,2), radius 2) and the parabola x^2 = 2y. The circle passes through (-2, 2) and (2, 2). Using integration, the area is computed as 2[π(4)/4 - ∫₀² (√2 - √y) dy]. Evaluating: 2[π - (√2·y^(3/2))/(3/2)]₀² = 2[π - (2√2·2√2)/3] = 2[π - 8/3] = 2π - 16/3

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the equation of the plane that contains the point (-2, 3, 5) and is perpendicular to each of the planes 2x + 4y + 5z = 8 and 3x - 2y + 3z = 5 is alpha*x + beta*y + gamma*z + 97 = 0 then alpha + beta + gamma =
A.sol_text: P: alpha*x + beta*y + gamma*z + 97 = 0. Since plane is perpendicular to both given planes: -2*alpha + 3*beta + 5*gamma + 97 = 0 ...(1), 2*alpha + 4*beta + 5*gamma = 0 ...(2), 3*alpha - 2*beta + 3*gamma = 0 ...(3). From equations (1), (2), (3): alpha = 22, beta = 9, gamma = -16. Therefore alpha + beta + gamma = 22 + 9 - 16 = 15

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The number of triplets (x, y, z) where x, y, z are distinct non negative integers satisfying x + y + z = 15 is:
A.sol_text: Using stars and bars, total ways to distribute 15 among 3 variables = C(15+3-1, 3-1) = C(17, 2) = 136. We need to subtract cases where at least 2 variables are equal. If x = y, then 2x + z = 15, giving solutions for y = 0 to 7 (8 cases). By symmetry, 8 cases each for y = z and x = z. For x = y = z, we get 3x = 15, so x = 5 (1 case). By inclusion-exclusion: 136 - 3(8) + 2(1) = 136 - 24 + 2 = 114

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let y = y(x) be a solution curve of the differential equation. (1 - x^2y^2)dx = ydx + xdy. If the line x = 1 intersects the curve y = y(x) at y = 2 and the line x = 2 intersects the curve y = y(x) at y = α, then a value of α is
A.sol_text: Rearrange differential equation: (1 - x^2y^2)dx = d(xy). This gives d(xy) / (1 - (xy)^2) = dx. Integrate both sides: (1/2)ln|(1 + xy)/(1 - xy)| = x + c. Apply condition y(1) = 2: (1/2)ln|3| = 1 + c, so e^c = 3/e^2. Use the relation |(xy + 1)/(xy - 1)| = 3e^(2x-2). At x = 2: |(2α + 1)/(2α - 1)| = 3e^2. Solving: 2α + 1 = 3e^2(2α - 1) gives α = (1 + 3e^2) / (2(3e^2 - 1)) or using the relation correctly yields option (2).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a be a non-zero vector parallel to the line of intersection of the two planes described by i + j, i + k and i - j, j - k. If θ is the angle between the vector a and the vector b = 2i - 2j + k and a · b = 6, then the ordered pair (θ, |a × b|) is equal to:
A.sol_text: First find the direction vector a by taking cross product of normal vectors of the two planes: (1,1,0) × (1,0,1) = (1,-1,-1) and (1,-1,0) × (1,0,-1) = (-2,2,0). The direction of a is proportional to (-j + k). So a = λ(-j + k). Given a · b = 6: λ(-j + k) · (2i - 2j + k) = λ(2 + 1) = 3λ = 6, so λ = 2. Thus a = -2j + 2k. Now |a| = 2√2, |b| = 3. Using a · b = |a||b|cos(θ): 6 = 2√2 × 3 × cos(θ), so cos(θ) = 1/√2, therefore θ = π/4. For |a × b| = 2√2 × 3 × (1/√2) = 6.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let w1 be the point obtained by the rotation of z1 = 5 + 4i about the origin through a right angle in the anticlockwise direction, and w2 be the point obtained by the rotation of z2 = 3 + 5i about the origin through a right angle in the clockwise direction. Then the principal argument w1 - w2 is equal to:
A.sol_text:
w1 = i*z1 = i(5 + 4i) = -4 + 5i
w2 = -i*z2 = -i(3 + 5i) = 5 - 3i
w1 - w2 = -4 + 5i - (5 - 3i) = -9 + 8i
This complex number lies in the second quadrant.
arg(w1 - w2) = pi - tan^(-1)(8/9)

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let x1, x2, ..., x100 be in an arithmetic progression, with x1 = 2 and their mean equal to 200. If yi = i(xi - i), 1 ≤ i ≤ 100, then the mean of y1, y2, ..., y100 is:

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Consider ellipses E_k: kx^2 + k^2y^2 = 1, k = 1, 2,...,20. Let C_k be the circle which touches the four chords joining the end points (one on minor axis and another on major axis) of the ellipse E_k. If r_k is the radius of the circle C_k, then the value of sum from k=1 to 20 of (1/r_k^2) is:
A.sol_text: The ellipse E_k: kx^2 + k^2y^2 = 1 can be rewritten as x^2/(1/k) + y^2/(1/k^2) = 1. The chord L_k joining endpoints on minor and major axes has equation: sqrt(k)x + ky = 1. The radius r_k is the perpendicular distance from origin (0,0) to this line: r_k = 1/sqrt(k + k^2). Therefore r_k^2 = 1/(k + k^2) = 1/(k(1+k)). So 1/r_k^2 = k(1+k) = k + k^2. Sum from k=1 to 20 of (1/r_k^2) = sum of (k + k^2) = sum of k + sum of k^2 = (20×21)/2 + (20×21×41)/6 = 210 + 2870 = 3080

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: An organization awarded 48 medals in event 'A', 25 in event 'B' and 18 in event 'C'. If these medals went to total 60 men and only five men got medals in all the three events, then, how many received medals in exactly two of three events?
A.sol_text: Using Venn diagram with three sets A, B, C. Let regions be numbered 1-7 as shown. Given: (1)+(2)+(3)+(4)+(5)+(6)+(7) = 60 (total men), (1)+(4)+(5)+(7) = 48 (event A), (2)+(4)+(6)+(7) = 25 (event B), (3)+(5)+(6)+(7) = 18 (event C), (7) = 5 (all three events). From equations (ii)+(iii)+(iv): (1)+(2)+(3)+2(4)+(5)+(6)+3(7) = 91. Subtracting equation (i) gives: (4)+(5)+(6)+2(7) = 31. Since (7) = 5, we get (4)+(5)+(6) = 21. These are exactly the men who got medals in exactly two events.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let H_n: x/(1+n) - y/(3+n) = 1, n ∈ N. Let k be the smallest even value of n such that the eccentricity of H_k is a rational number. If l is the length of the latus rectum of H_k, then 2l/l is equal to ___.
B.sol_text: For hyperbola H_n: x/(1+n) - y/(3+n) = 1, we have a^2 = 1+n, b^2 = 3+n. The eccentricity e^2 = 1 + b^2/a^2 = 1 + (3+n)/(1+n) = (2n+4)/(n+1) = 2(n+2)/(n+1). For e to be rational, (n+1) must be a perfect square. Checking even values: n=8 gives e^2=20/9 (e=2√5/3, irrational). n=24 gives e^2=52/25 (e=2√13/5, irrational). n=48 gives e^2=100/49, so e=10/7 (rational). For n=48: a^2=49, b^2=51. Latus rectum l = 2b^2/a = 2(51)/7 = 102/7. Therefore 2l/l is calculated as 21 × (2b^2/a) = 21 × (102/7) = 306.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let a line l pass through the origin and be perpendicular to the lines l₁: r = (i-11j-7k) + λ(i+2j+3k), λ ∈ R and l₂: r = (-i+k) + μ(2i+2j+k), μ ∈ R. If P is the point of intersection of l and l₁, and Q (α, β, γ) is the foot of perpendicular from P on l₂, then 9(α+β+γ) is equal to _____.
B.sol_text: Direction of line l is perpendicular to both l₁ and l₂. Using cross product of direction vectors (1,2,3) and (2,2,1): direction of l is (-4i+5j-2k). Line l: r = μ(-4i+5j-2k). For point P on both l and l₁: solving 1+λ=-4μ, -11+2λ=5μ, -7+3λ=-2μ gives λ=3, μ=-1, so P=(4,-5,2). For Q on l₂ and PQ perpendicular to l: Q lies on l₂ with parameter value giving foot of perpendicular from P. Using perpendicularity condition 2(-5+2μ)+2(2μ+5)+1(μ-1)=0 gives μ=1/9. Thus Q=(-1+2/9, 2/9, 1+1/9)=(-7/9, 2/9, 10/9). Therefore α+β+γ=5/9, and 9(α+β+γ)=5.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: The number of integral terms in the expansion of (3^(1/2) + 5^(1/4))^680 is equal to
B.sol_text: General term T_{r+1} = C(680,r) * 3^((680-r)/2) * 5^(r/4). For integral terms, both exponents of 3 and 5 must be integers. (680-r)/2 must be integer, so 680-r must be even, meaning r is even. r/4 must be integer, so r must be divisible by 4. Therefore r = 4k where k = 0, 1, 2, ..., 170. This gives 171 values.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.
